author: Jane Austen
text: Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him. She told the story, however, with great spirit among her friends; for she had a lively, playful disposition, which delighted in anything ridiculous.
mock_answer: Darcy has just snubbed Elizabeth at the ball, and rather than sulk she turns the insult into a funny story for her friends. The passage sets up her wit and pride against his aloofness.

author: Jane Austen
text: Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him.
mock_answer: Mr. Darcy is the wealthy, reserved friend of Mr. Bingley who has just arrived in the neighbourhood. Elizabeth Bennet is the second Bennet daughter, quick-witted and observant; Darcy has just declined to dance with her.

author: Jane Austen
text: Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him.
mock_answer: A rich young man, Mr. Bingley, has rented Netherfield near the Bennet family. Mrs. Bennet hopes he will marry one of her five daughters. At the first ball Bingley is charming, but his friend Darcy is proud and slights Elizabeth.

author: Jane Austen
text: It is a truth universally acknowledged, that a single man in possession of a good fortune, must be in want of a wife.
mock_answer: C'est une vérité universellement reconnue qu'un célibataire pourvu d'une belle fortune doit avoir envie de se marier.

author: Jane Austen
text: Mr. Darcy walked off; and Elizabeth remained with no very cordial feelings towards him.
mock_answer: ダーシー氏は立ち去り、エリザベスは彼に対してあまり好意的ではない気持ちのまま残された。

author: Herman Melville
text: Call me Ishmael. Some years ago—never mind how long precisely—having little or no money in my purse, and nothing particular to interest me on shore, I thought I would sail about a little and see the watery part of the world.
mock_answer: The narrator introduces himself as Ishmael and explains that restlessness and an empty purse are pushing him to sea. The casual tone hides a deeper melancholy he will admit to shortly.

author: Franz Kafka
text: As Gregor Samsa awoke one morning from uneasy dreams he found himself transformed in his bed into a gigantic insect.
mock_answer: Gregor Samsa is the protagonist, a travelling salesman who supports his parents and sister. This is the opening line, so nothing else is known about him yet except that he has just woken up as an insect.
